x: The Regulating Act, 1773 set up the first Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta (it began in 1774). The Charter Acts of 1813 and 1833 and the 1858 Act came later and did not create it.
t: Link the first Supreme Court to the earliest regulating legislation.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Charter Act, 1833 created the post of Governor-General of India, and Bentinck merely happened to be its first holder.
t: Separate the legal change (A) from the person who held the post (R).

x: Charter Act 1853 – open competition for Civil Services; 1858 Act – Canning as first Viceroy; 1909 Act – separate electorate for Muslims; 1919 Act – direct elections. Option B swaps the 1853 and 1858 features.
t: Anchor each Act to its signature first-time feature.

x: First meeting (9 Dec 1946), Objectives Resolution moved (13 Dec 1946), adopted (22 Jan 1947), Constitution adopted (26 Nov 1949): B, C, D, A. A resolution is moved before it is adopted, which rules out A and D.
t: Order by dates; moving precedes adopting.

x: I, II and III are correct: the First Amendment, 1951 added the Ninth Schedule, Article 15(4) and Articles 31A–31B. IV is wrong: the parliamentary form came from Great Britain and was in the original Constitution, not added by an amendment.
t: Spot the statement that describes something no amendment introduced.
s:
Consider the following statements about the First Amendment Act, 1951:
I. It added the Ninth Schedule.
II. It added clause (4) to Article 15.
III. It added Articles 31A and 31B.
IV. It introduced the parliamentary form of government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the parliamentary form of government began in Great Britain and the presidential form in the USA.
t: Match each form of government to its country of origin.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The parliamentary form of government was first introduced in Great Britain.
Statement B: The presidential form was first formed in the USA.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Both are true and R explains A: the first joint sitting (1961) was called to resolve a deadlock over the Dowry Prohibition Bill.
t: Ask whether R gives the occasion for the event in A.

x: PAC – first set up in 1921; Estimates Committee – 1950; Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee – 1997, the first in any Indian legislature; Lok Sabha Ethics Committee – 2000. The Rajya Sabha committee came before the Lok Sabha one.
t: Arrange the four committees by year, then match.

x: Both are true and R explains A: judicial review is credited to the USA because it was first laid down in Marbury v. Madison (1803).
t: Check whether the case in R is the origin claimed in A.

x: I, II and III are correct (Kesavananda Bharati 1973; Shankari Prasad; Hussainara Khatoon as first PIL). IV is wrong: the Federal Court was inaugurated on 1 October 1937 under the 1935 Act; 1950 is when the Supreme Court replaced it.
t: Find the date that belongs to a different institution.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Basic Structure doctrine was first propounded in Kesavananda Bharati in 1973.
II. Fundamental Rights were first held amendable in the Shankari Prasad case.
III. The first PIL considered was Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar.
IV. The Federal Court was inaugurated in 1950.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: NHRC – Justice Ranganath Misra (1993); first Law Commission of independent India – M.C. Setalvad (1955); Election Commission – Sukumar Sen; Planning Commission Deputy Chairman – Gulzarilal Nanda. Option A swaps Setalvad and Sukumar Sen.
t: Match each 'first head' to the body's field: law, elections, rights, planning.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct (parties recognised in 1985 by the 52nd Amendment; Tamil the first classical language; Madras the first municipal corporation, 1688). Statement 4 is wrong: Rajasthan (Nagaur, 1959) was first in Panchayati Raj and Andhra Pradesh second.
t: Check the 'first state' claim: first and second are often swapped.

x: Community Development Programme (1952), National Extension Service (1953), Panchayati Raj at Nagaur (2 October 1959), constitutional recognition of parties (1985): A, B, C, D.
t: Fix each year; the CDP precedes the NES by one year.

x: The first Supreme Court at Fort William opened in 1774 with Sir Elijah Impey as first Chief Justice; Macaulay was the first Law Member; Section 87 of the Charter Act, 1833 opened Company service to Indians without discrimination of religion or colour.
t: Separate the year, the judge, the Law Member and the provision.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 1853 Act separated the Council's legislative and executive functions and also introduced open competition for Civil Services — two separate features of the same Act.
t: Two features of one Act do not explain each other.

x: All three are correct: the Indian Councils Act, 1909 first associated Indians with the Executive Councils of the Viceroy and the Governors, and S.P. Sinha became the first Indian Law Member of the Viceroy's Council.
t: Recall the 1909 'firsts' for Indians in executive councils.

x: The 1909 Act is the Morley-Minto reforms, Lord Minto the 'Father of Communal Electorate', the 1919 Act the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms, and the separate electorate for Muslims a feature of the 1909 Act.
t: Pair each Act with its popular name, then place Minto and the electorate.

x: All three are correct: the 1919 Act first made the Central Legislature bicameral, introduced dyarchy in the provinces and used the term 'responsible government'.
t: Recall the three 'firsts' of the Montagu-Chelmsford Act.

x: All four are correct: the 1935 Act provided for an All-India Federation, which never came into being, and dyarchy at the Centre, which was never implemented.
t: Remember that 1935 proposed both features but neither took effect.

x: The 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy and set up the Federal Court, inaugurated on 1 October 1937 with Sir Maurice Gwyer as its first Chief Justice; the Supreme Court replaced it on 26 January 1950.
t: Link each Act or court to its date or first holder; start with the unmistakable Gwyer pair.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Government of India Act, 1935
(b) Federal Court
(c) Sir Maurice Gwyer
(d) Supreme Court of India

List-II
(i) Inaugurated on 1 October 1937
(ii) Abolished dyarchy in the provinces
(iii) First Chief Justice of the Federal Court
(iv) Replaced the Federal Court in 1950

Which of the following is the correct code?

x: Both are true: the Government of India Act, 1935 created Sindh and Orissa as new provinces.
t: Recall the two provinces created in 1935.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Government of India Act, 1935 created Sindh as a new province.
Statement B: The Government of India Act, 1935 created Orissa as a new province.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Under the 1935 Act residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General — not in the Federal Court, the Executive Council or the provincial Governors. (Under the Constitution they lie with Parliament.)
t: Remember who held residuary powers before the Constitution.

x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea (1934); the Swaraj Party made the first formal demand at its Ranchi conference, held in May 1934; the Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946.
t: Separate the idea, the formal demand and the constituting plan.

x: All four are correct: Sachchidananda Sinha presided temporarily at the first meeting, Rajendra Prasad became permanent President on 11 December 1946, Frank Anthony was the first temporary Deputy Chairman and H.C. Mukherjee the first permanent Vice-President.
t: Keep temporary and permanent office-holders apart.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:

I. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President of its first meeting.
II. Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the permanent elected Chairman or President on 11 December 1946.
III. Frank Anthony was the first nominated temporary Deputy Chairman.
IV. H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the Objectives Resolution was moved at the fifth meeting of the first session, and H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President.
t: Check the meeting number and the office separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Objectives Resolution was moved at the fifth meeting of the first session of the Constituent Assembly.
Statement B: H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Both are true but unrelated: B.N. Rau drafting the first version does not explain why the Constitution came fully into force on 26 January 1950 (chosen to mark Purna Swaraj Day, 1930).
t: Ask whether R gives the cause of the date in A.

x: The Constituent Assembly had 15 women members. 12, 18 and 21 are close distractors.
t: Recall the exact number of women members.

x: I to IV are correct: the Interim Government was announced on 24 August 1946 and took charge on 2 September 1946 with Nehru as Vice-President of the Executive Council; R.K. Shanmukham Chetty was independent India's first Finance Minister. V is wrong: John Mathai succeeded him in 1948.
t: Separate the first Finance Minister from his successor; check each Interim Government date.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Interim Government of 1946:

I. It was announced on 24 August 1946.
II. It took charge on 2 September 1946.
III. Jawaharlal Nehru was the Vice-President of the Executive Council.
IV. R.K. Shanmukham Chetty was the first Finance Minister of independent India.
V. John Mathai was the first Finance Minister of independent India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the Constitution of India Bill, 1895 made the first explicit demand for Fundamental Rights; the First Amendment, 1951 restricted Article 19 rights, and the First Schedule lists the States and UTs.
t: Check each part of a compound statement separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Constitution of India Bill of 1895 made the first explicit demand for Fundamental Rights.
Statement B: The First Amendment Act, 1951 restricted the rights under Article 19, while the First Schedule lists the States and Union Territories.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Rajendra Prasad – first President (from Bihar); Pratibha Patil – first woman President; Droupadi Murmu – first tribal woman President; S. Radhakrishnan – first Vice-President. The trap is confusing 'first woman' with 'first tribal woman'.
t: Separate 'first woman' from 'first tribal woman'.

x: Sardar Patel was the first Deputy PM; Indira Gandhi was the first PM who was a Rajya Sabha member when appointed (1966); J.B. Kripalani moved the first no-confidence motion against Nehru in 1963; G.V. Mavalankar was the first Lok Sabha Speaker.
t: Match each leader to the parliamentary 'first' tied to that person.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
(b) Indira Gandhi
(c) Acharya J.B. Kripalani
(d) G.V. Mavalankar

List-II
(i) First Deputy Prime Minister of India
(ii) First Prime Minister who was a Rajya Sabha member at the time of appointment
(iii) Moved the first no-confidence motion, against Nehru's government in 1963
(iv) First Speaker of the Lok Sabha

x: I and II are correct: the first Lok Sabha election was in 1951–52 and the First Lok Sabha's first session began on 13 May 1952. III is wrong: 9 December 1946 was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly.
t: Spot the date that belongs to the Constituent Assembly.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The first general election to the Lok Sabha was held in 1951–52.
II. The first session of the First Lok Sabha began on 13 May 1952.
III. The first session of the First Lok Sabha began on 9 December 1946.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Nargis Dutt was the first actress nominated to the Rajya Sabha, in 1980; the Leader of the Opposition was first recognised in the Lok Sabha in 1969.
t: Separate the person, her year and the 1969 recognition.

x: The Chamber of Princes had 120 members, was created under the Government of India Act, 1919, and its first Chancellor was Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner.
t: Recall the size, the Act and the first Chancellor.

x: The PAC was first set up in 1921 under the 1919 Act; the Federal Court was established under the 1935 Act; Sir Maurice Gwyer was its first Chief Justice.
t: Link each body to the Act that created it.

x: Both are true: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court in 1989 and was also the first Muslim woman in the higher judiciary.
t: Recall both 'firsts' of Fathima Beevi.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court in 1989.
Statement B: Justice M. Fathima Beevi was the first Muslim woman in the higher judiciary.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor (United Provinces, 1947), Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister (Uttar Pradesh, 1963), Indira Gandhi the first woman PM (1966) and Meira Kumar the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker (2009).
t: Do not swap the first woman Governor and the first woman Chief Minister.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Sarojini Naidu
(b) Sucheta Kripalani
(c) Indira Gandhi
(d) Meira Kumar

List-II
(i) First woman Governor of a State
(ii) First woman Chief Minister of a State
(iii) First woman Prime Minister of India
(iv) First woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha

x: A is true: the first President's Rule was imposed in Punjab on 20 June 1951. R is false: President's Rule (State Emergency) is imposed under Article 356; Article 352 deals with National Emergency.
t: Separate Article 352 (National Emergency) from Article 356 (President's Rule).
s:
Assertion (A): President's Rule was imposed for the first time in Punjab in 1951.
Reason (R): President's Rule in a State is imposed under Article 352 of the Constitution.

x: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 under K.C. Neogy, as required by Article 280. Its report followed in 1952, the tempting distractor.
t: Separate the year of constitution from the year of the first report.
s: In which year was the First Finance Commission constituted?

x: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 with K.C. Neogy as Chairman. Nehru was the first (ex-officio) Chairman of the Planning Commission and Arvind Panagariya the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog.
t: Pair each planning or finance body with its first head and year.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Year the First Finance Commission was constituted
(b) First Chairman of the Finance Commission
(c) First Chairman of the Planning Commission
(d) First Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog

List-II
(i) 1951
(ii) K.C. Neogy
(iii) Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru
(iv) Arvind Panagariya

x: Both are true: the Inter-State Council was set up by a Presidential order in 1990, following the Sarkaria Commission, under the power Article 263 gives the President.
t: Recall the Article and commission behind the Inter-State Council.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Inter-State Council was first set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission.
Statement B: The Inter-State Council is set up by the President under Article 263.

Which of the following is correct?

x: All four are correct: the Ombudsman began in Sweden (1809); the First ARC (1966) recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas, and Morarji Desai submitted its interim report on them.
t: Verify the origin year and the ARC's recommendation and author.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809.
II. The First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in 1966.
III. The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas.
IV. Morarji Desai submitted the interim report of the First Administrative Reforms Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true but unrelated: the first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968, while Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal only in 2019 under the 2013 Act.
t: A later appointment cannot explain an earlier Bill.

x: Odisha passed the first Lokayukta Act (1970), but Maharashtra, with its 1971 Act, was the first State to set up a working Lokayukta (1972). 1968 is the year of the first Lokpal Bill, the distractor.
t: Separate passing an Act (Odisha) from setting up the institution (Maharashtra).
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Maharashtra
(b) Year Maharashtra enacted its Lokayukta law
(c) Odisha

List-II
(i) 1971
(ii) First state to pass a Lokayukta Act
(iii) First state to set up a working Lokayukta
(iv) 1968

x: The first NHRC Chairman took office in 1993; the first Law Commission of independent India dates from 1955; the Public Service Commission was provided by the 1919 Act and set up on 1 October 1926.
t: Separate the legal basis (1919 Act) from the date of setting up (1926).

x: Sukumar Sen – CEC 1950–58; V.S. Ramadevi – first woman CEC; 61st Amendment – voting age lowered to 18; 1989 general election – first held at that age.
t: Link the amendment to the change and the change to its first election.

x: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland on 4 September 2013 — not in a general election.
t: Recall the by-election, not a national poll.

x: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election, Nagaland, on 4 September 2013. The 1989 election is linked to the voting age of 18 and 1961 to the first joint sitting.
t: Eliminate options tied to other electoral 'firsts'.

x: The 52nd Amendment (1985) gave parties constitutional recognition through the Tenth Schedule; Shyama Prasad Mukherjee was the first President of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and Vajpayee the first BJP President, in 1980.
t: Separate the Jana Sangh's founder from the BJP's first President.

x: Both are true: the First Official Language Commission was set up in 1955 under B.G. Kher.
t: Recall the year and the head of the Official Language Commission.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The First Official Language Commission was established in 1955.
Statement B: B.G. Kher headed the First Official Language Commission.

Which of the following is correct?

x: All three are correct: Madras had India's first Municipal Corporation (1688); Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959; Madhya Pradesh was first to implement the 73rd Amendment in its true spirit.
t: Check each local-government 'first' separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The first Municipal Corporation in India was established at Madras in 1688.
II. Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur by Jawaharlal Nehru.
III. Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the 73rd Amendment in its true spirit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The Community Development Programme (1952) was the first major rural development programme after independence; the National Extension Service followed in 1953 and Panchayati Raj in 1959.
t: Pick the earliest programme in the rural-development sequence.

x: G.V. Mavalankar was the first Lok Sabha Speaker; Vithalbhai Patel was the first elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly (1925); Rajendra Prasad was the Constituent Assembly's permanent President and Sachchidananda Sinha its temporary President.
t: Separate the temporary and permanent Presidents, and the 1925 and 1952 Speakers.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Speaker of the Lok Sabha
(b) First elected President (Speaker) of the Central Legislative Assembly, 1925
(c) First permanent elected President of the Constituent Assembly
(d) Temporary President at the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly

List-II
(i) G.V. Mavalankar
(ii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(iii) Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
(iv) Vithalbhai Patel

x: Ninth Schedule – First Amendment; Federal Court – 1 October 1937; first PIL considered – Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979); Sukumar Sen – CEC from 1950 to 1958.
t: Match each item to the only clue of its kind: an amendment, a date, a case, a tenure.

x: Under the Regulating Act, 1773 the Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal, and Warren Hastings was the first. Cornwallis came later; Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (1833) and Canning the first Viceroy (1858).
t: Keep the titles apart: of Bengal (1773), of India (1833), Viceroy (1858).

x: The Charter Act, 1853 introduced open competition for the Civil Services. The 1833 Act only declared Indians eligible (Section 87); the 1858 Act transferred rule to the Crown.
t: Distinguish eligibility (1833) from open competition (1853).

x: The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred rule from the Company to the Crown and made the Governor-General the Viceroy. The 1861 and 1919 Acts reformed councils; 1947 ended British rule.
t: Link the end of Company rule to the Act after the 1857 revolt.

x: B is incorrect: the Charter Act, 1813 ended the Company's monopoly in India only partly, keeping the tea and China trade (fully ended in 1833). It also allowed missionaries and granted ₹1 lakh a year for education.
t: Watch absolute words like 'completely'.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: R describes what the 1935 Act later did, which cannot explain why dyarchy was introduced in 1919.
t: A later Act cannot be the reason for an earlier one.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the 42nd Amendment is called the 'Mini-Constitution' because it made sweeping changes, such as adding Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) and Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.
t: Ask whether R gives the scale of change behind the nickname.

x: Both are true: the 1919 Act introduced direct elections and bicameralism at the Centre and separated Central and Provincial budgets.
t: Recall the 1919 Act's central-level features.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections and bicameralism at the Centre.
Statement B: The Government of India Act, 1919 separated Central and Provincial budgets.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Both are true: the 1935 Act set up the Federal Court (working from 1937), and the Indian Independence Act, 1947 created two Dominions, India and Pakistan.
t: Check each Act's feature separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Government of India Act, 1935 established the Federal Court in 1937.
Statement B: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 created two independent Dominions, India and Pakistan.

Which of the following is correct?

x: I and II are correct: the 52nd Amendment (1985) brought the anti-defection law and the Tenth Schedule. III is wrong: the NJAC was created by the 99th Amendment (2014).
t: Spot the feature that belongs to a different amendment.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 52nd Amendment enacted the Anti-Defection Law.
II. The 52nd Amendment inserted the 10th Schedule.
III. The 52nd Amendment created the National Judicial Appointments Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: I, II and III are correct (73rd – Panchayats; 74th – Municipalities; 86th – Article 51A(k)). IV is wrong: the 84th Amendment froze seat allocation on the 1971 Census until 2026, not 2030.
t: Check the cut-off year of the seat freeze.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj.
II. The 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to Municipalities.
III. The 86th Amendment inserted Article 51A(k) regarding education of children.
IV. The 84th Amendment froze Lok Sabha seat allocations based on the 1971 Census up to 2030.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Regulating Act 1773 – Supreme Court at Calcutta; Pitt's India Act 1784 – Dual Control; Charter Act 1813 – monopoly partly abolished; Charter Act 1833 – Company lost its commercial role entirely.
t: Arrange the Company's decline: partial (1813) then complete (1833).

x: Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 – NHRC, SHRCs and Human Rights Courts; RTI Act 2005 – right supporting transparency and accountability; Lokpal Act 2013 – five-member Selection Committee; RPA 1951 – registration of parties by the ECI.
t: Match each Act to the body or right it creates.

x: Charter Act 1813, Indian Councils Act 1909, Government of India Act 1919, Government of India Act 1935: B, C, D, A.
t: Order the Acts by their years.

x: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774). Canning, Bentinck and Cornwallis were Governors-General, not judges.
t: Separate judicial posts from executive ones.

x: I and II are correct: the Regulating Act banned both private trade and bribes by Company officials. III contradicts I, so it is wrong.
t: Two statements that contradict each other cannot both be true.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Act of 1786 gave the Governor-General two separate powers — to override his Council and to act as Commander-in-Chief.
t: Two powers from one Act do not explain each other.

x: Lord Cornwallis was the first to use the powers given by the Act of 1786 — that is why the Act was passed, as he made it a condition of taking office.
t: Link the 1786 Act to the Governor-General it was made for.

x: The Charter Act was enacted in 1833; under it the Governor-General of Bengal became Governor-General of India; Lord William Bentinck was the first; a fourth member was added as Law Member.
t: Match the year, the new title, the person and the new member.

x: A is true and B is false: Section 87 of the Charter Act, 1833 barred discrimination in Company service on grounds of religion, birth or colour; it did not introduce discrimination.
t: Opposite statements: only one can be true.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Section 87 of the Charter Act of 1833 barred discrimination in Company service.
Statement B: Section 87 of the Charter Act of 1833 introduced discrimination in Company service.

Which of the following is correct?

x: The Charter Act, 1853 clearly separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council. Making the Governor-General of India was the 1833 Act; the Secretary of State came in 1858; the 1861 Act restored Bombay and Madras' powers.
t: Link each option to its Act and pick the 1853 one.

x: All four are correct: the 1858 Act made Canning Viceroy, abolished the Board of Control and Court of Directors, and created the Secretary of State for India with a 15-member Council.
t: Recall the 1858 changes in London and in India.

x: Both are true: the Indian Councils Act, 1861 began Indian participation in law-making (by nominating Indians to the council).
t: Recall the year and the first step of Indian participation.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Indian Councils Act was enacted in 1861.
Statement B: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 initiated Indian participation in law-making.

Which of the following is correct?

x: All three are correct: the 1861 Act restored the legislative powers of Bombay and Madras, a step towards decentralisation.
t: Recall which presidencies regained law-making powers.

x: The Indian Councils Act, 1861 gave the Viceroy power to issue Ordinances (and introduced the portfolio system). It is the forerunner of the President's ordinance power.
t: Link the Ordinance power to the 1861 Act.

x: A Viceroy's Ordinance under the 1861 Act could stay in force for up to six months.
t: Recall the six-month limit.

x: A is incorrect: the Indian Councils Act of 1892 was enacted in 1892, not 1909 (1909 is the Morley-Minto Act). The 1892 Act brought indirect election, Budget discussion without voting, and questions with six days' notice but no supplementaries.
t: Check the year attached to the Act's name.

x: 1909 Act – supplementary questions allowed; S.P. Sinha – first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council; 1919 Act – Chamber of Princes; 1935 Act – Maurice Gwyer as Federal Court Chief Justice.
t: Pair each Act with its own feature, then place the person.

x: The 1919 Act is the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms; the Morley-Minto Reforms were the 1909 Act.
t: Pair the Act with the Secretary of State and Viceroy of its time.

x: All four are correct: the 1935 Act proposed an All-India Federation and Central Dyarchy, neither implemented, and its Section 42 is the model for the President's Ordinance power under Article 123.
t: Remember the 1935 proposals that never came into force.

x: Both are true: the Indian Independence Act, 1947 ended British sovereignty and gave the Constituent Assemblies both constitution-making and legislative powers.
t: Recall the dual role given to the Constituent Assembly.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Indian Independence Act ended British sovereignty.
Statement B: The Act gave the Constituent Assemblies dual constitution-making and legislative powers.

Which of the following is correct?

x: All seven are correct: the 1909 Act had no dyarchy or provincial autonomy and an enlarged unicameral central legislature; the 1919 Act began separating subjects and extended communal representation; the 1935 Act kept that and proposed a bicameral Federal Legislature.
t: Compare the three Acts feature by feature.

x: Both are true: neither the 1909 nor the 1919 Act created a new court; the existing High Courts remained the judicial bodies. The Federal Court came only with the 1935 Act.
t: Remember the Federal Court came only in 1935.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 had existing High Courts as its judicial body.
Statement B: The Government of India Act of 1919 had existing High Courts as its judicial body.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the date of enactment (1978) is not explained by what the Amendment did (undoing Emergency-era changes).
t: An Amendment's content does not explain its year.

x: All four are correct: the 52nd Amendment amended Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191 to bring in disqualification on grounds of defection.
t: Recall the four Articles on vacancy and disqualification.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 52nd Amendment amended Article 101.
II. The 52nd Amendment amended Article 102.
III. The 52nd Amendment amended Article 190.
IV. The 52nd Amendment amended Article 191.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the 91st Amendment (2003) tightened anti-defection rules and capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the House.
t: Recall the two changes of the 91st Amendment.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The 91st Amendment was enacted in 2003.
Statement B: The 91st Amendment strengthened anti-defection provisions and limited the size of the Council of Ministers.

Which of the following is correct?
